focus.jnote: The environment improved overnight. After Wednesday’s Fed hold and Thursday’s war-driven rout, the tape staged a sharp rebound: Amazon reported blowout Q2 results — revenue $200.6B (+20% YoY) beating ~$196.5B, and AWS up 36.7% to $42.2B, its fastest growth in 18 quarters — and shares jumped ~11–12% pre-market, following Microsoft’s Azure-driven surge. Apple, by contrast, fell ~7% on soft China/Services. On the macro side, June core PCE cooled to 3.3% year-over-year (just 0.1% month-over-month, below the 0.2% expected) as a brief Iran truce pulled energy prices lower. Critically, there was no fresh U.S.–Iran escalation overnight — oil eased and stayed near $84 WTI — and South Korea’s KOSPI surged ~14–18% to a record, reinforcing a global risk-on tone. The catch: the 30-year Treasury yield is still near its highest since 2007 and core inflation remains well above 2%, so this is a relief rally, not an all-clear.
focus.notdown: AI/AWS-levered mega-cap tech (AMZN, MSFT) and the chip complex (MU, SNDK) are the clear bid — Amazon’s AWS acceleration and Microsoft’s Azure print revived confidence that AI capex is monetizing, and Korean chip names logged a record session. The scanner boarded exactly one Type A name (AMZN, bullish). But note the data flag on that row and the still-live oil/bond backdrop — strength is real but not risk-free.
focus.notup: Apple (−7% on soft China/Services) and rate-sensitive long-duration names pressured by a 2007-high long bond are the day’s laggards. But selling bear calls into a sharp AI-driven relief rally — with a record KOSPI and futures green — carries obvious squeeze risk. No bearish name was boarded; the disciplined stance is watch-only on the downside.
focus.why: Why YELLOW, not GREEN? Composite eased to 44 (MILD) and P(≥1% gap) dropped to ~30% (below the 35% trigger), which technically clears the GREEN locks. But two things hold it at YELLOW: (1) the macro tail is only paused, not gone — the U.S.–Iran war is in a fragile truce, WTI is still ~$84, and the 30Y yield sits near a 2007 high, any of which can gap the tape on a headline; and (2) the single boarded candidate carries a data-integrity conflict (scanner logged a “miss” on a name that actually crushed estimates), an independent reason to slow down. Half size, A-grade only, and prefer waiting for the 9:35 validation before committing new premium.

risks: Iran truce is fragile — the war is paused, not resolved; reports note Strait of Hormuz traffic began to falter on renewed friction. Any re-escalation sends crude and the whole tape gapping instantly — the week’s biggest tail.

30-year Treasury yield near a 2007 high — the long bond stayed elevated even after a cooler PCE, and Chair Warsh signaled the Fed welcomes higher yields. A further spike pressures long-duration tech even amid the AI bid.

Inflation still above target — June core PCE cooled to 3.3% but remains well over the Fed’s 2% goal, and the data predates July’s oil rebound; three FOMC members dissented for a hike. Renewed energy pressure could revive rate fear.
XOM / CVX earnings today — energy majors report into a war-driven but easing-oil tape; Exxon already missed on maintenance costs. Single-stock energy gap risk plus a two-sided oil bid.
ISM Manufacturing · Mon 8/3 — the next scheduled macro checkpoint after this week’s Fed/PCE/mega-cap cluster; a weak or hot print into a still-jittery bond market could reset sentiment.
